TITLE: Tax Act 2003
ACTNUMBER: 2003 No 47
TYPE: Act
STATUS: In force
VERSION: Latest
VERSIONTITLE: as at 17 September 2026
AGENCY: the Ministry of Finance & Revenue
DATEOFASSENT: 18 December 2003
COMMENCEMENT: see section 2
NOTE: This consolidated Act deliberately preserves extensive inserted numbering accumulated through successive taxation amendments. Lettered provisions occur in recurring groups throughout the Act, including provisions inserted between existing lettered provisions. The resulting numbering reflects amendment history rather than a clean renumbering exercise.

PARTNUMBER: 1
PARTTITLE: Preliminary and Interpretation
AMENDMENT: Part 1 has been amended on multiple occasions between 2005 and 2026, including consequential amendments arising from taxation, customs, environmental, digital economy, and public finance legislation.
SECTION: 1
HEADING: Liability arising from transaction — preliminary and interpretation
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of preliminary and interpretation where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
AMENDMENT: Section 1 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 17E inserted on 1 April 2014 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

AMENDMENT: Section 22E inserted on 1 April 2024 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 22F
HEADING: Exemptions and exclusions — inserted treatment of preliminary and interpretation
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of preliminary and interpretation where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.

HEADING: Treatment of associated persons — inserted treatment of preliminary and interpretation
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of preliminary and interpretation where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

SECTION: 31E
HEADING: Exemptions and exclusions — inserted treatment of preliminary and interpretation
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of preliminary and interpretation where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;

   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

SECTION: 34FA
HEADING: Interaction with other provisions — inserted treatment of preliminary and interpretation

   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
AMENDMENT: Section 40 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 41
HEADING: Consequential treatment — administration and commissioner powers
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of administration and commissioner powers where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.

SECTION: 47
HEADING: Special rule for prescribed arrangements — administration and commissioner powers
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of administration and commissioner powers where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.

8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 54B inserted on 1 April 2022 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 54C
HEADING: Timing of liability — inserted treatment of administration and commissioner powers
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of administration and commissioner powers where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

SECTION: 67
HEADING: Interaction with other provisions — administration and commissioner powers
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of administration and commissioner powers where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 70 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 84C inserted on 1 April 2011 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.

5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
AMENDMENT: Section 100 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 107
HEADING: Election or notification — taxpayer registration and identification
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of taxpayer registration and identification where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
AMENDMENT: Section 107 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.

SECTION: 109C
HEADING: Corrections and adjustments — inserted treatment of taxpayer registration and identification
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of taxpayer registration and identification where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
AMENDMENT: Section 112 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 113
HEADING: Commissioner determination — taxpayer registration and identification
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of taxpayer registration and identification where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.

SECTION: 118
HEADING: Election or notification — taxpayer registration and identification
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of taxpayer registration and identification where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 121D inserted on 1 April 2020 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 121EA
HEADING: Consequential treatment — inserted treatment of income and assessable amounts
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of income and assessable amounts where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 138 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 139
HEADING: Consequential treatment — income and assessable amounts
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of income and assessable amounts where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.

1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of income and assessable amounts where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 149CB inserted on 1 April 2026 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;

4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
