Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 1098 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
AMENDMENT: Section 1103 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1106B inserted on 1 April 2011 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1122BA inserted on 1 April 2022 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 1122C
HEADING: Exemptions and exclusions — inserted treatment of tax avoidance, evasion, concealment, and integrity measures
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of tax avoidance, evasion, concealment, and integrity measures where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.

   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1134B inserted on 1 April 2020 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
AMENDMENT: Section 1138 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1139
HEADING: Election or notification — returns assessments and reassessments
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of returns assessments and reassessments where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.

3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.

11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1146BC inserted on 1 April 2022 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 1146C
HEADING: Exemptions and exclusions — inserted treatment of returns assessments and reassessments
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of returns assessments and reassessments where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.

10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
AMENDMENT: Section 1153 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1153B
HEADING: Special rule for prescribed arrangements — inserted treatment of returns assessments and reassessments
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of returns assessments and reassessments where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1153B inserted on 1 April 2014 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1156C inserted on 1 April 2011 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 1156D
HEADING: Commissioner determination — inserted treatment of returns assessments and reassessments
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of returns assessments and reassessments where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 1166 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1173E inserted on 1 April 2026 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 1175
HEADING: Commissioner determination — returns assessments and reassessments
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of returns assessments and reassessments where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 1175 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
AMENDMENT: Section 1182 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1182B
HEADING: Anti-avoidance interaction — inserted treatment of returns assessments and reassessments
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of returns assessments and reassessments where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.

SECTION: 1186B
HEADING: Timing of liability — inserted treatment of returns assessments and reassessments
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of returns assessments and reassessments where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1190C inserted on 1 April 2026 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 1197
HEADING: Records and evidence — payments credits refunds and remissions
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of payments credits refunds and remissions where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 1202 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1203
HEADING: Special rule for prescribed arrangements — payments credits refunds and remissions
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of payments credits refunds and remissions where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.

   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
AMENDMENT: Section 1212 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1212B
HEADING: Anti-avoidance interaction — inserted treatment of payments credits refunds and remissions
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of payments credits refunds and remissions where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 1218 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1219

   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;

5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

SECTION: 1238
HEADING: Anti-avoidance interaction — payments credits refunds and remissions
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of payments credits refunds and remissions where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 1238 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.

   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 1252 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1253
HEADING: Anti-avoidance interaction — payments credits refunds and remissions
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of payments credits refunds and remissions where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.

4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
AMENDMENT: Section 1262 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1263
HEADING: Election or notification — interest penalties and defaults
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of interest penalties and defaults where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
