9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1272DB inserted on 1 April 2026 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 1272E
HEADING: Records and evidence — inserted treatment of interest penalties and defaults
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of interest penalties and defaults where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;

4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
AMENDMENT: Section 1279 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of interest penalties and defaults where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
AMENDMENT: Section 1287 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.

1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of interest penalties and defaults where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.

5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.

SECTION: 1304
HEADING: Amount to be included — interest penalties and defaults
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of interest penalties and defaults where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

SECTION: 1311
HEADING: Exemptions and exclusions — interest penalties and defaults
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of interest penalties and defaults where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.

4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
AMENDMENT: Section 1318 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1323
HEADING: Election or notification — audits investigations and information
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of audits investigations and information where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
AMENDMENT: Section 1323 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.

SECTION: 1342
HEADING: Exemptions and exclusions — audits investigations and information
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of audits investigations and information where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;

AMENDMENT: Section 1348 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1349
HEADING: Timing of liability — audits investigations and information
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of audits investigations and information where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.

   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.

SECTION: 1357E
HEADING: Election or notification — inserted treatment of audits investigations and information
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of audits investigations and information where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 1365 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1366
HEADING: Anti-avoidance interaction — audits investigations and information
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of audits investigations and information where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;

SECTION: 1371
HEADING: Consequential treatment — audits investigations and information
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of audits investigations and information where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.

AMENDMENT: Section 1377E inserted on 1 April 2026 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 1378
HEADING: Records and evidence — audits investigations and information
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of audits investigations and information where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.

SECTION: 1391
HEADING: Interaction with other provisions — confidentiality disclosure and data matching
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of confidentiality disclosure and data matching where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.

6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1398D inserted on 1 April 2026 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1403D inserted on 1 April 2024 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 1404
HEADING: Exemptions and exclusions — confidentiality disclosure and data matching
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of confidentiality disclosure and data matching where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
AMENDMENT: Section 1404 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
AMENDMENT: Section 1407 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1408
HEADING: Consequential treatment — confidentiality disclosure and data matching
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of confidentiality disclosure and data matching where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;

   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1411H inserted on 1 April 2008 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 1412
HEADING: Application of general rule — confidentiality disclosure and data matching
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of confidentiality disclosure and data matching where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;

5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

SECTION: 1425
HEADING: Application of general rule — confidentiality disclosure and data matching
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of confidentiality disclosure and data matching where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
AMENDMENT: Section 1425 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and

11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.

2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1446B inserted on 1 April 2014 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 1451 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.
