SECTION: 1458C
HEADING: Election or notification — inserted treatment of digital services and electronically supplied activities
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of digital services and electronically supplied activities where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;

8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.

8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1471B inserted on 1 April 2026 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 1471C
HEADING: Application of general rule — inserted treatment of digital services and electronically supplied activities
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of digital services and electronically supplied activities where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

SECTION: 1478
HEADING: Commissioner determination — digital services and electronically supplied activities
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of digital services and electronically supplied activities where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.

   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.

SECTION: 1483
HEADING: Exemptions and exclusions — digital services and electronically supplied activities
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of digital services and electronically supplied activities where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.

   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.

AMENDMENT: Section 1503 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1504
HEADING: Liability arising from transaction — objections reviews and appeals
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of objections reviews and appeals where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.

8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1507H inserted on 1 April 2008 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 1508
HEADING: Apportionment — objections reviews and appeals
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of objections reviews and appeals where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;

   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.

   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.

2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

SECTION: 1536C
HEADING: Exemptions and exclusions — inserted treatment of objections reviews and appeals
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of objections reviews and appeals where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;

8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1541B inserted on 1 April 2026 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.

SECTION: 1547
HEADING: Anti-avoidance interaction — objections reviews and appeals
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of objections reviews and appeals where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 1558 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
AMENDMENT: Section 1566 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1566B
HEADING: Apportionment — inserted treatment of debt recovery and enforcement
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of debt recovery and enforcement where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

SECTION: 1571EC
HEADING: Records and evidence — inserted treatment of debt recovery and enforcement
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of debt recovery and enforcement where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

AMENDMENT: Section 1573 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1574
HEADING: Treatment of associated persons — debt recovery and enforcement
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of debt recovery and enforcement where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.

8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.

4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

SECTION: 1590
HEADING: Interaction with other provisions — debt recovery and enforcement
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of debt recovery and enforcement where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
AMENDMENT: Section 1590 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

SECTION: 1596G
HEADING: Treatment of associated persons — inserted treatment of debt recovery and enforcement
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of debt recovery and enforcement where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.

   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 1600 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1601
HEADING: Special rule for prescribed arrangements — debt recovery and enforcement
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of debt recovery and enforcement where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.

4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
AMENDMENT: Section 1616 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1616B
HEADING: Apportionment — inserted treatment of debt recovery and enforcement
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of debt recovery and enforcement where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.

8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.

   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
