11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
AMENDMENT: Section 1640 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1641
HEADING: Anti-avoidance interaction — insolvency liquidation and recovery
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of insolvency liquidation and recovery where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 1641 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1646CA inserted on 1 April 2017 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 1646D
HEADING: Special rule for prescribed arrangements — inserted treatment of insolvency liquidation and recovery
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of insolvency liquidation and recovery where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.

5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

SECTION: 1655
HEADING: Corrections and adjustments — insolvency liquidation and recovery
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of insolvency liquidation and recovery where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.

5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1660DC inserted on 1 April 2020 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.

9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1676E inserted on 1 April 2022 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 1676F
HEADING: Amount to be included — inserted treatment of insolvency liquidation and recovery
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of insolvency liquidation and recovery where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1681DB inserted on 1 April 2008 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

SECTION: 1681E
HEADING: Special rule for prescribed arrangements — inserted treatment of insolvency liquidation and recovery
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of insolvency liquidation and recovery where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.

5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
AMENDMENT: Section 1698 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
AMENDMENT: Section 1703 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1704
HEADING: Corrections and adjustments — charities public bodies and exemptions
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of charities public bodies and exemptions where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.

SECTION: 1716
HEADING: Election or notification — charities public bodies and exemptions
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of charities public bodies and exemptions where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.

AMENDMENT: Section 1722 has been amended by 1 or more enactments, including consequential amendments made after its original commencement.

SECTION: 1722BC
HEADING: Consequential treatment — inserted treatment of charities public bodies and exemptions
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of charities public bodies and exemptions where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
AMENDMENT: Section 1726CA inserted on 1 April 2008 by an amending Act and subsequently modified by consequential legislation.

   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.

9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.

SECTION: 1744D

1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of agriculture fisheries and primary industries where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.

   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

SECTION: 1751CC
HEADING: Timing of liability — inserted treatment of agriculture fisheries and primary industries
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of agriculture fisheries and primary industries where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and

7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.

10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.

   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.

5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.

   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

SECTION: 1764H
HEADING: Records and evidence — inserted treatment of agriculture fisheries and primary industries
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of agriculture fisheries and primary industries where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.

4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;

SECTION: 1778
HEADING: Application of general rule — agriculture fisheries and primary industries
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of agriculture fisheries and primary industries where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.

2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.

   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;

SECTION: 1792C
HEADING: Treatment of associated persons — inserted treatment of resource extraction, water use, and environmental effects
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of resource extraction, water use, and environmental effects where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.

Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.

3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
7. The Commissioner may require further particulars if the information supplied does not reasonably establish the basis on which the person has treated the amount, and may specify the form, manner, period, or electronic method by which the particulars are to be provided.
8. A determination made under this section does not, merely because it is made for administrative purposes, alter the substantive liability imposed by another provision of this Act.
9. If a later amendment affects the operation of this section, the amendment applies according to its commencement provision, subject to any savings or transitional rule and without reopening a completed period except where this Act expressly permits reassessment.
10. Nothing in this section prevents the application of a specific charging provision, anti-avoidance provision, withholding provision, or recovery provision that is expressed to operate independently of the general rule.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;
   (b) the amount is not already taken into account under another charging provision;
   (c) the treatment is consistent with any applicable election or prescribed method; and
   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.

SECTION: 1804
HEADING: Consequential treatment — resource extraction, water use, and environmental effects
1. This section applies for the purposes of determining the treatment of resource extraction, water use, and environmental effects where an amount, transaction, arrangement, supply, activity, person, or event is required to be taken into account under this Act.
2. The amount or matter must be determined for the relevant period by applying this Act as a whole, subject to any provision that expressly modifies, excludes, defers, attributes, or replaces the ordinary rule.
3. If more than 1 provision could apply, the provisions must be read together so far as practicable, but a provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. A person claiming an exemption, deduction, credit, remission, threshold, concession, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must hold records sufficient to establish every fact on which that treatment depends.
5. For the purposes of subsection 4, records may include contracts, invoices, ledgers, electronic records, declarations, certificates, valuations, correspondence, system logs, or other material reasonably capable of establishing the relevant facts.
6. Where an amount relates partly to matters within and partly outside the operation of this provision, the amount must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis having regard to the purpose for which the expenditure was incurred, the nature of the transaction, and the extent to which each part relates to the taxable activity.
   (a) the transaction has a direct connection with the matter to which this section applies;

   (d) the application of the paragraph does not defeat an express limitation elsewhere in this Act.
11. The person must notify the Commissioner of a material change in circumstances within the period prescribed by regulations, and the notification must identify the transaction, period, amount, persons affected, and provision relied on.
12. The Commissioner may make consequential adjustments to prevent duplication, omission, unintended timing advantages, or inconsistent treatment between related provisions, but must give written reasons where the adjustment materially increases liability.
